meta.curriculum_anchor: CEFR (primary); Adult ESOL Core Curriculum 2001 (secondary, UK functional context)
meta.mapping_convention: curriculum/empirical convention (locked): E1=A1, E2=A1/A2, E3=A2, L1=B1, L2=B2. NB the SQA/UK NARIC qualification-award chart sits one level higher from E2 up; state the convention on any certification-facing equivalence claim.
meta.rarpa_bank_note: Five representative objectives per skill domain per level are included here for build use; the full bank of eight per domain per level is in analysis/rarpa_objectives.md.
flags: [FLAG FOR EXPERT REVIEW: DELTA practitioner] validate can-do selection, grammar sequencing, vocabulary load, objective challenge
[FLAG FOR EXPERT REVIEW: funding specialist] confirm objectives meet GLA RARPA expectations

can_do.listening: Recognise familiar words and very basic phrases about self, family and immediate surroundings when speech is slow and clear.
can_do.reading: Understand familiar names, words and very simple sentences on notices, posters and forms.
can_do.spoken_interaction: Interact simply if the other person repeats or rephrases slowly; ask and answer simple questions on immediate need.
can_do.spoken_production: Use simple phrases to describe where I live and people I know.
can_do.writing: Write simple isolated phrases and sentences; fill in a form with personal details.

anchor_triggers: no response or L1-only response to an English prompt
immersion_triggers: intelligible on-topic English across consecutive turns without requesting L1
E1.retention_encounters: 8-14 encounters per item for receptive knowledge
E1.reinforcement_interval: expanding by calendar time: ~1 day, then ~3 days, then ~1-2 weeks, shorten on lapse

speaking_listening: By the end of week 4, I can introduce myself by saying my name, my country and my first language in a spoken exchange.
By the end of week 6, I can make a GP appointment in a roleplay by giving my name, date of birth and one reason for the visit.
By week 6, I can ask 'how much is it?' and say the price back when shopping in a roleplay.
By the end of the unit, I can respond to five everyday spoken questions about my family with single words or short phrases.
By week 5, I can follow three simple spoken instructions in a roleplay.
reading: By week 4, I can recognise and point to my name, date of birth and address on a simple form.
By the end of the unit, I can read ten everyday signs and say what each one means.
By week 5, I can find the date and time on a simple appointment letter or card.
By week 6, I can match five written words to the correct picture.
By the end of the unit, I can read the numbers 1 to 100 and say a price on a label.
writing: By week 4, I can write my full name, date of birth and nationality on a simple form.
By the end of the unit, I can copy my address accurately into the correct field of a form.
By week 6, I can write three short phrases about myself.
By the end of the unit, I can fill in a simple registration form with my personal details.
By the end of the unit, I can write a one-line message saying I cannot come to an appointment.

can_do.listening: Understand high-frequency phrases and catch the main point in short, clear, simple messages and announcements.
can_do.reading: Read short simple texts; find predictable information in everyday material.
can_do.spoken_interaction: Handle short routine exchanges of information on familiar topics.
can_do.spoken_production: Use a series of phrases to describe family, living conditions, background and recent job.
can_do.writing: Write a series of simple phrases and sentences linked with and, but, because; short notes and messages.

grammar_targets: past simple of to be and regular past
anchor_triggers: L1-only response to an English prompt
immersion_triggers: mixed L1/English completing the task with support
E2.reinforcement_interval: expanding by calendar time from ~1 day

speaking_listening: By week 6, I can describe my family in four or five linked spoken sentences using and, but, because.
By week 5, I can report a simple housing repair in a roleplay, saying what is broken and where.
By the end of the unit, I can ask and answer at least five questions about a daily routine.
By week 6, I can explain why I missed an appointment using the past simple.
By week 4, I can catch the main point of a short spoken announcement and say what it was about.
reading: By week 5, I can find the price, date and place in a short advert or leaflet.
By the end of the unit, I can read a short text message and say what action it asks me to take.
By week 6, I can read a simple appointment letter and say the date, time and sender.
By week 4, I can find a time, platform or price in a timetable.
By the end of the unit, I can read three-to-four-step instructions and put them in order.
writing: By week 6, I can write three to four sentences about my family linked with simple connectors.
By week 5, I can write a short note to my child's teacher to say my child is ill.
By the end of the unit, I can complete a form with personal details and one short written answer.
By week 6, I can write a short message to report a repair.
By the end of the unit, I can write four sentences about my present or recent job.

can_do.listening: Understand phrases and the main point in short clear messages on areas of immediate relevance.
can_do.reading: Find specific information in everyday material; understand short simple personal letters.
can_do.spoken_interaction: Communicate in simple routine tasks; manage short social exchanges.
can_do.spoken_production: Describe in simple terms family, living conditions, education and job.
can_do.writing: Write short simple connected text and a simple personal letter.

grammar_targets: modals of advice and obligation (should, must, have to)

speaking_listening: By the end of the unit, I can describe a past event in six or more spoken sentences using the past simple.
By week 6, I can give and respond to advice in a roleplay using should and have to.
By the end of the course, I can register my child at a school in a roleplay, giving the information requested and asking one question.
By week 5, I can explain a problem with a bill or letter and ask what to do next.
By week 6, I can describe my plans for next week using going to and will.
reading: By the end of the unit, I can read a short personal letter or email and answer three questions about it.
By week 6, I can find gross pay, a named deduction and net pay on a payslip.
By the end of the course, I can read a short public-service notice and say what I need to do and by when.
By the end of the unit, I can skim a short text and say what it is mainly about.
By week 5, I can read an email from a GP or school and identify the action and the deadline.
writing: By the end of the unit, I can write a short connected text of six or more sentences about a past experience.
By week 6, I can write a short personal email asking for information from a service.
By the end of the course, I can write a message reporting a problem and requesting a specific action.
By the end of the unit, I can complete a longer form including a short free-text reason.
By the end of the course, I can write a reply to a school email confirming attendance and asking one question.

can_do.listening: Understand the main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters in work, school and leisure.
can_do.reading: Understand high-frequency everyday and job-related texts and descriptions of feelings in personal letters.
can_do.spoken_interaction: Deal with most situations while travelling; enter unprepared into conversation on familiar topics.
can_do.spoken_production: Connect phrases to describe experiences and hopes; briefly give reasons and explanations.
can_do.writing: Write straightforward connected text on familiar topics; personal letters describing experiences.

L1.reinforcement_interval: expanding by calendar time, longer gaps for well-learned items

speaking_listening: By the end of the course, I can explain a problem with a service and negotiate a resolution in a roleplay, sustaining at least eight turns.
By week 6, I can give reasons and explanations for a decision using a range of connectors.
By the end of the course, I can handle a bank-account-opening roleplay, answering questions and querying anything unclear.
By week 8, I can take part in an unprepared conversation on a familiar topic and ask follow-up questions.
By week 6, I can use the present perfect to talk about my experience since arriving in the UK.
reading: By the end of the course, I can read an official text and explain its main points in my own words.
By week 8, I can read a payslip or tenancy agreement and explain each main section.
By the end of the unit, I can identify the writer's purpose and main argument in a short factual text.
By week 6, I can read an official email and identify the request and any implied deadline.
By the end of the unit, I can read guidelines and identify what I must, should and must not do.
writing: By the end of the course, I can write a connected text of three or more paragraphs on a familiar topic.
By week 6, I can write a formal email of complaint stating the problem, the impact and the action I want.
By the end of the course, I can write a reply to an official email answering each point raised.
By the end of the unit, I can write clear instructions for a multi-step process.
By week 8, I can write a short text giving reasons for and against a choice.

can_do.listening: Follow extended speech and complex argument on reasonably familiar topics; most TV news and current affairs.
can_do.reading: Read articles and reports with particular viewpoints; understand contemporary prose.
can_do.spoken_interaction: Interact with fluency and spontaneity; take an active part in discussion, sustaining views.
can_do.spoken_production: Give clear detailed descriptions; explain a viewpoint with advantages and disadvantages.
can_do.writing: Write clear detailed text, an essay or report giving reasons for or against a viewpoint.

grammar_targets: full conditional range incl. third conditional
L2.reinforcement_interval: expanding by calendar time, long gaps for mastered items

speaking_listening: By the end of the course, I can present a viewpoint on a topical issue, giving advantages and disadvantages.
By week 8, I can take an active part in a discussion, accounting for and sustaining my views.
By week 6, I can challenge a decision in a formal roleplay, stating my grounds.
By the end of the unit, I can give a clear, detailed spoken description of a process.
By week 6, I can interview-practise, answering competency questions with structured examples.
reading: By the end of the course, I can read an article that takes a viewpoint and identify the stance and supporting points.
By week 8, I can read a contract or formal policy and explain my rights and obligations.
By the end of the unit, I can distinguish fact from opinion in contemporary writing.
By week 6, I can read two articles on the same issue and compare their arguments.
By the end of the unit, I can locate and synthesise information from across a long text.
writing: By the end of the course, I can write a clear, detailed essay or report giving reasons for or against a viewpoint.
By week 8, I can write a formal letter highlighting the personal significance of an event.
By the end of the unit, I can write a structured argument with introduction, body and conclusion.
By week 6, I can write a covering message for a job application tailored to the role.
By the end of the unit, I can redraft my own writing to improve clarity and cohesion after feedback.
